In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, characterization and structural properties of a series of new coordination polymers based on the 5-hydroxyl group of hip ligands.
the design and synthesis of new metal–organic frameworks based on hip ligands.
the synthesis of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) based on the 5-hydroxylisophthalic acid ligand and the investigation of their structural, magnetic and luminescent properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the title compound crystallizes as a three-dimensional framework with a 3D hydrogen bond network.
the title compound is a three-dimensional coordination polymer with an unusual hip ligand and an unprecedented coordination number of 9 for a hip ligand.

the title compound crystallizes as a 3D coordination polymer, in which the 5-hydroxyl groups of the hip anions are not involved in hydrogen bonding, and the 3D framework structure is stabilized by O—H⎯⎯⋯O and C—H⋅⋅⎯⎷⋯O bonds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the hip ligands can form a three-dimensional framework with different metal ions, such as CoIII, NiII, CuII, MnII, ZnII, CdII, LaIII and YIII, which are coordinated by bpy ligands and water molecules.
the hip ligand can be a good bridging ligand in constructing a metal–organic framework (MOF) with the help of a co-ligand.
the hip ligand is a versatile building block for the formation of metal–organic frameworks with different dimensionalities and topologies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 2D structure is formed by hip ligands and the 2,2'-bipyridine ligand, while the hip ligands are connected by the DyIII ions to form the 2D layer.
the DyIII ion is able to form a three-dimensional framework, which is a very rare example in the field of metal–organic frameworks.
the 5-hydroxyl group in the 5-hy- droxyisophthalic acid is not a good hydrogen-bond donor, which is in contrast with the 5-halogeno- isophthalates.
